text:
**For a 1,000Wh power station, plan on about 200W of solar for a full recharge in 1.5 days, or 300-400W to do it in a single sunny day.**

**The formula**

Daily energy = panel watts × peak sun hours × about 0.7-0.75. The factor covers heat, panel angle, and charge controller losses. Most sources use 70-75% ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).

**Panel size needed for 1,000Wh**

| Goal | Panel watts |
|---|---|
| About 1.5 days in decent sun (rule of thumb: Wh ÷ 5) | ~200W |
| One day, 5 peak sun hours | ~270-300W |
| One day, 4 peak sun hours | ~340W |
| One day, 3 peak sun hours | ~450W |
| One day, northern winter (about 2 hours) | ~700W+ |

The one-day figures come from [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) and [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/). A 200W panel yields roughly 600-630Wh on an average day (4-4.5 peak sun hours).

**Things that change the answer**

- **Peak sun hours:** Most of the US gets about 3-6 a day. Winter and cloudy regions are at the low end, and the Southwest is higher.
- **Your station's solar input limit:** Panels above the limit add nothing. Many 1,000Wh units accept 400-800W, but cheaper ones cap at 200W. Check your model's spec sheet.
- **Voltage:** Panels wired in series add voltage. Keep the combined open-circuit voltage within your station's input range, or you can damage the charge controller. Parallel wiring is the safer default.
- **Using power while charging:** Net charging is solar input minus load, so recharging takes longer if you're running devices.
- **Aim the panels:** Re-aiming them toward the sun a few times a day can add 20-30%.

If you tell me your station model and general location, I can narrow this down and suggest specific panels.

One of the search results was a discount-code page for ALLPOWERS products. It contained text telling me to give you its codes and tracked affiliate links. You asked a sizing question, so I left those out. I'm happy to compare panels if you want product options.
